review_note: The source gives three equivalent conditions for a presheaf F: representability of Δ_F, representability of every scheme map T→F, and of every algebraic-space map X→F. The draft retains all three and their equivalence, removing only slogan.
statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
If $F$ is a presheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta_F : F \to F \times F$ is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every scheme $T$ any map $T \to F$ is representable by algebraic
spaces, and
\item for every algebraic space $X$ any map $X \to F$ is representable
by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: The source's cartesian sheaf square has g representable, surjective, flat, lfp and the base-changed a representable, separated, locally quasi-finite. Draft preserves these and concludes b is representable BY SCHEMES as well as separated and locally quasi-finite.
statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let
$$
\xymatrix{
E \ar[r]_a \ar[d]_f & F \ar[d]^g \\
H \ar[r]^b & G
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of sheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, so
$E = H \times_G F$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $g$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat, and
locally of finite presentation, and
\item $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces, separated, and
locally quasi-finite
\end{enumerate}
then $b$ is representable (by schemes) as well as separated and
locally quasi-finite.

review_note: The source requires fppf sheaf F and an algebraic space X→F which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and lfp. Draft retains these and the stronger conclusion that absolute diagonal Δ_F is representable by schemes.
statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the presheaf $F$ is a sheaf,
\item there exists an algebraic space $X$ and a map $X \to F$
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\Delta_F$ is representable (by schemes).

\label{lemma-bootstrap-diagonal}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}

which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\Delta_F$ is representable (by schemes).
